definition: The price row where the session spent the most time blocks so far, from a time-price opportunity profile built from the session's bars. Each bar is one time block and marks every row its range traversed; a row is the price rounded to a multiple of row_size.
boundaries: A tie between rows goes to the row nearest the middle of the session's range, then to the higher row. It counts time, not traded size, so it needs no volume; the volume point of control is point-of-control@1. The bar length is the block length, so bind it to 30-minute bars for the common profile. A session spanning more than max_rows rows is missing: max_rows bounds the block's state, so bind row_size to the instrument's tick size times the ticks per row. Bars without a time are missing. QML's unit runtime does not yet pass a bars input its time, so inside a unit this value stays missing until it does.
recognition: Price returning to the session's point of control reads as a return to value.

class_meanings.fx: No exchange session: the profile's day is the UTC slot session_start names, a choice, not a market fact.
